questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The University of Glasgow is the the fourth- oldest university in the English speaking world. The university is also in top 100 rank of best universities in the world. Despite the beautiful architecture of the building, the university is also known for graduates as Adam Smith, Kelvin and many more. The Law School is very known in Scotland, which is one of the reasons why I chose the University. The campuslife is also very nice and the university is known for hosting a lot of different activies to students of all kind. The academic opportunites and the modern and including spirit of the university was the reason why I chose it,.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The administration before the abroad experience was not good. Two weeks before the application to "study abroad for Erasmus students" the University told us that Erasmus students are not guaranteed to be accepted unless they have an accommodation in Glasgow. You couldn´t reach the university during this whole period. It was also difficult to contact them in relation to choosing courses for the semester. Despite all the experience and the administration was good.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The University sent us a form with all the important information about the city and the university before our arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy. Due to the accommodation crisis, I rented the flat for a whole academic year with a student who was going to study in Glasgow in the 1. semester. I was going to study there in the 2. semester.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The transportation system in Glasgow is not the best. The subway only goes from 6.30-23.21 from Mon Saturday. On Sundays, it opens at 10.00 and closes at 18.00. So if you want to go out too late you can´t take the subway and the buses are not reliable. But Uber works fine. So, if you don´t want to spend a lot of money on transportation then find a place on campus. It is also worth knowing that if you are under 22 years old you can get a free bus card in Scotland. This saves you a lot of money too. Despite this, the city center is good to live in and it's nice to live there when you are partying because it's close to Sauchiehall, which is the party street in Glasgow.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I noticed before the registration process was very stressfull due to the accomendation crisis in Glasgow. Despite that the registration process was easy and helpful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was online, and easy. But very slow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much. The administration did not answer the questions because of the lack of capacity. It took forever to get responses back. I contacted previous students to get the relevant documents for my registration processes.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I only got one course that I wanted due to the lack of capacity from the other courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it as soon as possible. And maybe contact other students for help. It may seem like a helpless procress, but when you are done then its worth it. The administration becomes very quick at responding and helping you as soon as you are accepted in the Uni. The University of Glasgow is a very good University and therefore would I recommend to trust the process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was a bit easier than I´m used to in my home university. There were a lot of reading in every lecture both essential and additional reading.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was not that different from my home institution. One course was online lectures with different videos from our professor. The two other courses worked as “Questions and Answers” in class. For each lecture, we got some questions to help us understand the lecture. We went through these in each class. The different thing was that I´m not used to having classes without any PowerPoint or other supplement to the class. The teaching style in one of my courses was a dialog with the teacher and the rest of the class without any PowerPoints and no breaks. I´m used to breaks in my home institution and we did not get any in Glasgow. This made the classes very long and it was different to concentrate the whole time.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Roman law of Property and obligations law, Criminal Justice and Contemporary issues in Healthcare law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Criminal Justice. If you are interested in criminal law then take this course. It gives you a good insight of the criminal justice system in UK and in Scotland.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A lot of ubers because the transportation system in Glasgow is not good when you are out late. From uni to the city center it costed around 12 pounds. It depends of course.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee, groceries and beer.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different social activites available. Glasgow Union (GUU) had all kinds of different clubs you could be a part of. They also had a very good and cheap kitchen where me and my friends used a lot. Nice food. GUU also had their own night clubs only for students. Very good. Close to the union was the "students only gym". I did not attend my self but I heard from others that it was very good and cheap.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel all over the country. It is a very beautiful country with nice people. The muserums are also free which is very nice.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do a highland trip and go to Isle of Sky and Glennfinnan (Harry potter bridge). It is unreal. There are also different kinds of islands you can go with your erasmus friends on the weekends. Also visit Edinburgh. It is an amazing city and only 1 hour by bus from Glasgow Burchanen Bus station.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Scottish people are very friendly and polite. They are willing to help you in every situation which is very nice. Denmark and Scotland are very similar countries and cultures which made it a lot easier to adjust. Just go to a pub and order a Tennant (beer) or an irn bru and then you have already adjusted to their culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a society or try to socialize with them in your class. Scottish people are very friendly and they are happy to show you around the city.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The food culture was a lot different from what I am used to. They also sell eggs outside of the fridge in the supermarket which also is weird.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their politeness and friendliness and the focus on students' mental and physical health

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Try Irn bru (their national drink)
2. Live close to Campus 
3. Explore Scotland (Highlands, other cities) in weekends

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting amazing new people from all over the world and exploring Scotland with them. I really love nature which also was one of the reasons why I chose the University. Scotland is known for their nature, so make sure to travel to the highlands and to Isle of Sky. Everything was just so nice about Scotland.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Understanding Scottish and the transportation system in Scotland.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.answer: Yes
